Study: spinal MRI

Indication: herniated disc

Findings:
The MRI of the lumbar spine reveals a broad-based posterior disc herniation at the L4-L5 level, causing moderate central spinal canal stenosis and impingement of the left L5 nerve root within the lateral recess. The disc herniation extends into the foraminal region, causing mild to moderate left foraminal narrowing. At the L3-L4 level, there is evidence of mild degenerative disc disease with minimal disc bulging, but no significant central or foraminal stenosis. At the L5-S1 level, the disc space is narrowed, and there is mild posterior disc bulge with mild facet arthropathy, but without significant nerve root compression. The conus medullaris is normal in appearance, terminating at the L1 level without evidence of abnormal signal changes. No areas of cord edema or myelomalacia are identified. The vertebral bodies show mild degenerative changes with scattered Schmalz nodes but no compression fractures or evidence of lytic or sclerotic lesions. The paraspinal soft tissues are unremarkable. The visualized portions of the sacroiliac joints do not show significant inflammatory changes. No evidence of epidural hematoma, infection, or abnormal fluid collections. The overall findings are consistent with lumbar spondylosis, with moderate canal stenosis at L4-L5 contributing to radicular symptoms.

Impression:
Broad-based posterior disc herniation at L4-L5 level causing moderate central spinal canal stenosis and impingement of the left L5 nerve root.
Mild to moderate left foraminal narrowing due to disc herniation extending into the foraminal region.
Mild degenerative disc disease at L3-L4 with minimal disc bulging, without significant stenosis.
Narrowed disc space at L5-S1 with mild posterior disc bulge and mild facet arthropathy, without significant nerve root compression.
Normal appearance of the conus medullaris terminating at L1, without abnormal signal changes.
Mild degenerative changes in vertebral bodies with scattered Schmalz nodes, no compression fractures or lytic sclerotic lesions.
Unremarkable paraspinal soft tissues and sacroiliac joints without significant inflammatory changes.
No evidence of epidural hematoma, infection, or abnormal fluid collections.
Findings consistent with lumbar spondylosis, with moderate canal stenosis at stenosis at L4-L5 contributing to radicular symptoms.
